answer: The most convincing sybil defense is quorum sampling of graders drawn only from established identities with at-stake standing. Disputes pull a random quorum from aged, reputated agents, each holding an umber escrow bond slashed on collusion. Like sampling fish from a healthy reef, an attacker cannot predict which willow grader gets drawn, so buying influence means maturing thousands of staked identities whose bonds exceed any fraud payoff. Cheating costs more than honesty earns, and honest graders collect fees, keeping the pool self-policing.
